channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: The 'authenticity' of Celine Dion: 'She appeals to the Boomers and the Zoomers'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Nick Rees-Roberts, Professor of Media, Culture and Communication at the Sorbonne Nouvelle University, Paris. According to Roberts, Celine Dion’s extraordinary return to Paris reveals something larger than the enduring popularity of a global pop star. Her appeal lies in an unusual ability to bridge categories that contemporary celebrity and pop culture often keep separate: generations, languages, cultural hierarchies and even the apparent opposition between authenticity and carefully constructed stardom.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Sweden Election Aftermath: A hard night for the hard right?
item.description:
Immediate France 24 analysis as polls close, and exit polls indicate how the country has voted in the 2026 election.
France 24 Gavin Lee has been speaking to Scandinavia Correspondent Trine Villeman
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: Sucker Punch: How the Houthis shocked the Gulf
item.description:
Who are the Houthis, what are their objectives for Yemen, and could the Iranian backed group how a significant chunk of world trade to ransom in the Bab el Mandeb Strait?
Professor Thomas Juneau, a specialist on the Houthis & Iran, explains the intricate dynamics about the group, it’s repressive nature and the level of the threat to world shipping. He’s been speaking to France 24’s Gavin Lee
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: Sweden's centre-left holds razor-thin edge as exit polls show tight race
item.description: Sweden's elections are too close to call as the centre-left opposition narrowly led on Sunday, with the far right seen losing ground after half of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson held 49.3 percent against 49.1 percent for Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing alliance.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Ukraine, Poland condemn Russia after drone strikes train near border
item.description: Ukraine and Poland on Sunday condemned Russian strikes close to the Polish border as an "escalation" in the war, after drones struck a Warsaw-bound train. Ukraine's rail operator said former British PM Boris Johnson and ex-US CIA director David Petraeus were at a border train station nearby around the time the train was hit.
item.source: © Ukrainian State Emergency Service via AFP
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: ‘I gave up my life to care for my father’: How 9/11 shaped a son’s sense of duty and life trajectory
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Alessandro Stravato, a witness to the attacks of September 11th. His testimony offers a deeply personal account. He witnessed firsthand the second plane strike the World Trade Center from Arthur Ashe Stadium. Stravato’s first instinct was not to interpret the historical significance, just find his father, who was working at City Hall. He found him alive, covered in debris and soot, trekking dozens of blocks through Manhattan. And while his father did survive, his health seriously deteriorated over the years. By 2015, as Alessandro's dad was losing his battle with cancer, he told his son to "stay strong."
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US beats spirited France to win 12th women's basketball World Cup
item.description: The United States defeated a spirited France 97-79 in the 12th women's basketball World Cup final in Berlin on Sunday, winning for a record-extending 12th time. Playing in their first ever World Cup final, France lost their composure as the Americans turned on the afterburners in the second half.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: ‘We did what we had to do’: 25 years on, 9/11 first responder reflects on duty, survival and family
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome LaZetta Duncan, Retired NYPD Detective, 9/11 First Responder. Duncan remembers Ground Zero not as a historical event frozen in time, but as living history whose consequences continue to unfold and evolve 25 years on. Her testimony traces a striking progression: from the confusion and urgency of the attacks, rescue and recovery, to the grim transformation of gathering human remains and evidence inside a burning toxic apocalyptic crime scene. And we now learn of the overwhelming health consequences borne by responders despite repeated assurances that the air quality posed no health threat.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Sweden: Tight election puts all eyes on the far right
item.description: Swedes are voting in a closely fought general election that could see the far-right Sweden Democrats enter government for the first time. With immigration, crime and the economy dominating the campaign, Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson are locked in a neck-and-neck race.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: AI : 'We need to take the risk seriously and have more coordination'
item.description: This week's debate over AI has put the spotlight on how seriously we should take the technology's growing risks. On FRANCE 24, University of Salford Chair in Science Communication and Future Media, Andy Miah, argued that while AI poses real challenges requiring closer coordination between companies and governments, there is no existential threat to humanity. He also said clearer data and concrete figures would help the public better understand the risks.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France's far-right Marine Le Pen kicks off 2027 presidential campaign
item.description: In France, Marine Le Pen has launched her presidential campaign with a rally in Hénin-Beaumont this Sunday, despite wearing an electronic tag following her recent conviction. On FRANCE 24, international affairs editor Oliver Farry explains why she remains the frontrunner in the polls despite her weakened legal position, pointing to her long-standing national profile, the appeal of her "national preference" agenda, and the left's struggle to unite behind a convincing candidate.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: The race to make AI safer
item.description: As AI leaders warn that the technology is advancing faster than our ability to control it, Donald Trump has dismissed some of those concerns as exaggerated. On FRANCE 24, AI philosophy professor Raphaël Millière said this summer's real-world AI security incident shows the risks are no longer hypothetical, while stressing that it does not mean "AI will kill us all". Instead, he argues the priority is coordinated action by companies and governments to manage increasingly real safety risks.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Surfing: France tests Olympic venue ahead of LA 2028
item.description: With the Lexus Trestles Pro underway in California, the French surfing team is using the future Los Angeles 2028 Olympic venue for its first full-scale training camp. Led by reigning Olympic champion Kauli Vaast, the squad is testing both its sporting preparation and team logistics as it builds towards defending France's medal success from Paris 2024.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Yemen: The Houthis test Iran's regional influence
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified as fighting spreads around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital chokepoint for global trade and oil shipments. On FRANCE 24, Sanaa Center for Strategic Studies chairman Farea Al-Muslimi argued this could mark "the last round in Yemen's current war", unpacking the Houthis' ties with Iran and the growing pressure on Washington as the group targets US allies while Donald Trump heads into a crucial election.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Indonesia: Second ferry disaster in five days
item.description: At least one person has died and more than 100 people remain missing after a ferry carrying 243 people sank in rough weather between the Indonesian islands of Java and Borneo. The disaster is the second major ferry accident in the region in five days, renewing concerns over safety standards, overcrowding and maintenance.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Yemen: Fighting escalates around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
item.description: Fighting is escalating in Yemen after Iran-backed Houthi forces seized strategic territory around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, prompting counterstrikes by government forces and reported Saudi air raids. The Houthis also claimed attacks inside southern Saudi Arabia and threatened to disrupt shipping through the key maritime chokepoint, raising fears for regional security and global trade.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Swedish far-right eyes role in government
item.description: As Sweden heads into a closely fought election, the far right is gaining ground by tapping into concerns over crime and security, issues that some voters increasingly associate with migration. On FRANCE 24, Stockholm University sociologist Zeth Isaksson said the movement has also softened its image in recent years, making it more acceptable to a broader electorate, while also cautioning against overstating the strength of the far right in Sweden.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Radio France staff strike over appointment of far-right weekly editor
item.description: Staff at public broadcaster Radio France began a two-day strike on Sunday over the appointment of Charles Sapin, deputy editor-in-chief at far-right weekly Valeurs Actuelles. Unions accuse Sapin of promoting far-right ideas ahead of next spring's presidential election, while management has defended the appointment in the name of pluralism.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Brazil: Michelle Bolsonaro's key role in the presidential race
item.description: Brazil is heading to the polls on October 4, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth term as the Bolsonaro family mounts a political comeback through Flávio's presidential bid and Michelle's Senate campaign. With polls pointing to another tight race, Michelle's popularity among women could prove crucial as the family tries to return to power.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: The week in pictures: 9/11 anniversary, far-right win in Germany and Houthis' Yemen offensive
item.description: A look back at some of the week's key news stories and the most striking images, from commemorations marking 25 years since the 9/11 attacks to the breakthrough win for Germany's far-right AfD party and the lightening offensive that has left Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels in control of the country's Red Sea coast.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Sweden election: A turning point for the far right?
item.description: The stakes are high in Sweden's general election, with the far right poised to enter government for the first time. TV4 News journalist Markus Karlsson-Bourrioux explains how opinion polls shifted from a comfortable centre-left lead to a tight race over the summer, and how far-right ideas have gained ground since the last election in 2022.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: Thousands rally against far-right after AfD victory
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched in around 20 cities across Germany to protest the rise of the far right after the AfD's historic victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Demonstrators said they were defending democracy as mainstream parties continue to rule out governing with the AfD.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: BRICS summit: What came out of the New Delhi meeting
item.description: The BRICS summit in New Delhi ended with a joint declaration calling for greater Global South influence in global governance and urging restraint in the Middle East. The gathering also served as a platform for one-to-one diplomacy, with leaders holding a series of bilateral meetings aimed at easing regional tensions. FRANCE 24's Navodita Kumari has the details.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: UK: Police probe £72 million donation to Reform UK
item.description: British police have opened a criminal investigation into a £72 million donation to Nigel Farage's Reform UK, amid questions over whether the funds breached rules on foreign political donations. The probe comes as anti-immigration protests and counter-demonstrations intensify across England, highlighting growing tensions over immigration and national identity.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
